heroHeadline: Farage Reclaims Clacton Seat as Burnham Government Marks a Month in Office
heroSubtitle: Nigel Farage won back his own Clacton seat on 13 August 2026 with 63.3% of the vote, a by-election he triggered himself on 7 July while facing scrutiny over a reported £5 million personal gift and other undeclared donations — but Reform UK's national polling has since slipped behind Labour, 25% to 28% in the latest Ipsos survey. The result caps a turbulent month for British politics that began when Andy Burnham was appointed Prime Minister on 20 July 2026, succeeding Keir Starmer and reshuffling the cabinet with John Healey as Chancellor, Ed Miliband as Foreign Secretary and Wes Streeting returning as Defence Secretary. The Bank of England has since held interest rates at 3.75% for a fifth straight meeting on 29 July, as CPI inflation eased to 2.6% in June even as energy prices stay volatile amid renewed Middle East tensions.
footerNote: Data sourced from UK Parliament Hansard, The National Archives, ONS, Bank of England, Electoral Commission, NHS England, BBC, Reuters, FT, The Guardian, Bloomberg, Al Jazeera, CNN, CNBC, ITV News, SPICe, and major academic institutions including LSE, Chatham House, and the Resolution Foundation.
